pricing.footnote: Pricing is not yet finalized. Follow the GitHub repo or the community forum for launch updates.

isItFree.a: Yes. Every core feature is free right now: reading, annotations, notes, whiteboards, AI chat (with a daily quota), vocabulary flashcards, forum, and the community book catalog. A paid Premium tier is planned for people who need bigger AI quotas, more storage, OCR, and X-Ray. Everything that's free today stays free.

copyright.q: Can I read any book on Pnyxy?
copyright.a: The built-in catalog only redistributes public-domain books (Project Gutenberg, Standard Ebooks, MEK). For copyrighted books you legally own (physical copies, PDFs you bought), you can either upload the file privately, or add a metadata-only "shell" entry and use notes, annotations, and community features against it without uploading anything. We do not host or distribute copyrighted material.

privacy.q: Who can see my notes and highlights?
privacy.a: Only you. Notes, annotations, bookmarks, and whiteboards are stored locally on your device and (if you're signed in) synced to your own Supabase row, protected by row-level security. Nothing you write is visible to other users unless you explicitly post it to the forum or share it.

ai.q: Does the AI train on my books or notes?
ai.a: No. When you use AI chat, the current page's text and your question are sent to the AI provider (OpenAI or Anthropic, depending on your settings) to generate a response. We don't train any model on user content, and the providers' own policies prohibit training on API traffic by default.

offline.a: Mostly. Once a book is opened it's cached locally, so you can read, annotate, and take notes without internet. AI chat, community forum, and book catalog search require a connection. Full offline mode (sync-later) is on the roadmap.

formats.a: PDF is the primary target, with full support for annotations, highlights, and AI reading. EPUB, plain text, and Markdown also render in the reader. MOBI is not supported (convert to EPUB first).

openSource.a: Yes. The code is MIT-licensed and on GitHub at github.com/LenYx24/pnyxy-reader. Issues, PRs, and forks are welcome. A separate repository hosts community themes and plugins that load into the app at runtime.

selfHost.a: Yes. The README has the full deployment guide. You'll need a Supabase project (free tier works), a Cloudflare Workers account for the web host, and API keys if you want the Pnyxy AI proxy. Desktop and mobile builds use Tauri and don't need any backend.

tutorial.title: Getting started with Pnyxy
tutorial.intro: Pnyxy is a reading + study app: bring your own books, talk to them with AI, and turn what you read into quizzes, vocabulary, and learning roadmaps. This page is a 5-minute walkthrough of the parts you'll actually use day to day.

quickStart.title: Quick start
quickStart.body: You can be reading inside a minute. Sign in is only required for cloud sync, AI quotas, and the social features — anonymous browsing of the catalog works without an account.

bullets.0: Sign in or create an account from the landing page (Google or email).
bullets.1: Open the Library and click "Upload" to add a PDF, or pick a free book from the Catalog.
bullets.2: Click the small "Open in reader" button on any uploaded book to jump straight into reading.
bullets.3: Drag a PDF / EPUB / TXT / Markdown file anywhere on the Library page to import it the fast way.

reading.title: Reading & annotating
reading.body: The reader supports PDF and EPUB. Select any text to mark it up, leave a note, or send it straight to AI — annotations sync across devices when signed in.

bullets.0: Highlight selected text in any color. The annotation panel collects every mark across the book for review.
bullets.1: Add a free-form comment to a highlight — useful for the "why does this matter" half of active reading.
bullets.2: Open the side notes pad for free-form text and whiteboard sketches that aren't tied to a specific passage.
bullets.3: Right-click a selection to translate it, look the word up, or send it to the AI chat with a citation back to the page.

aiChat.title: AI chat that knows your book
aiChat.body: The AI panel works in three modes: as a general assistant, anchored to a document (so its citations link back to specific pages), and tied to a roadmap (so it can edit the graph for you).

bullets.0: Pick the provider in the composer — Pnyxy's free quota, your own Anthropic key, or your OpenAI key.
bullets.1: When chat is started from a reader selection, replies use [p.42] tokens that link straight back to the page.
bullets.2: From any AI message, hit "Save as flashcards" to extract Q/A pairs into the vocabulary deck.
bullets.3: On a roadmap, click "Edit with AI" to chat about the graph — the model can add, remove, and reorder nodes live.

activeRecall.title: Quizzes, flashcards & vocabulary
activeRecall.body: Reading once isn't learning. Pnyxy turns content into spaced-repetition reviews so what you read sticks past the next exam.

bullets.0: Generate a quiz from a passage you uploaded — multiple choice, true/false, or short-answer.
bullets.1: Save flashcards from any AI answer or directly from a highlighted passage.
bullets.2: The Vocabulary tab is your word deck — words you looked up while reading get queued for review.
bullets.3: The Review screen runs the FSRS algorithm, so cards you struggle with come back sooner than ones you know.

planTrack.title: Roadmaps & streaks
planTrack.body: Plan a learning path, then keep the daily habit going. Roadmaps are directed graphs of topics; streaks are a 5-minute-a-day reading goal.

bullets.0: Generate a roadmap from a topic ("Linear algebra for ML") and the AI sketches a prerequisite-ordered set of nodes.
bullets.1: Enroll in a roadmap to project a finish date based on your weekly hours, then check off nodes as you go.
bullets.2: Streaks update automatically as long as you read for 5 minutes a day. The Streaks page shows the heatmap and your best streak.
bullets.3: Both surface as cards on Home and as items in the sidebar so you don't lose track of what you're working on.

community.title: Forum & community
community.body: Discussions and debates around books — early stage today, but the wiring is there. You can spin up a thread for any book in your library.

bullets.0: Each book has a "Discuss" tab with comments and replies.
bullets.1: The Forum index aggregates threads across every shared book.
bullets.2: Share an uploaded book with the community from the book card's 3-dot menu (PDF only, you keep ownership).

powerTips.title: Keyboard & navigation
powerTips.body: Once you've got the basics, these shortcuts make Pnyxy faster than clicking around.

bullets.0: Cmd/Ctrl + K — open the command palette: search across pages and your books, jump anywhere in one keystroke.
bullets.1: Cmd/Ctrl + , — open Settings (the universal Preferences hotkey).
bullets.2: Cmd/Ctrl + B — collapse or expand the sidebar.
bullets.3: Press ? anywhere outside an input — opens the cheatsheet listing every registered shortcut.
